column1: # ASSETS -- REFERENCE, not a log and not a count.
# Identity only: an id, a name, what kind of thing it is. NO QUANTITIES HERE.
# How many there are is derived from campaign/inventory.tsv (and, from phase 3b,
# from an inventory LOG); how much money moved for it is derived from
# campaign/money.tsv. This file exists so that both of those can NAME the same
# thing and be checked against each other.
# Reference, in the four-way taxonomy in dlwork/tooling_plan.md: it is
# hand-authored and has no upstream, so it can be WRONG but it cannot go STALE.
# *** THE SERVICE IDS ARE NOT A FUDGE. *** Money leaves the purse for things
# that are not goods -- wages, lodging, a licence, a loan. Double entry requires
# every money row to name SOMETHING, and without these the rule would be
# unsatisfiable and would get quietly broken on its first real use, which is how
# rules die. They are marked kind=service so `ledger.py` can tell them from
# goods and never look for them on a cart.
# weight + weight_unit, in two columns ON PURPOSE. The player's design, and
# it has teeth in 1e: DMG Appendix O counts encumbrance in GP WEIGHT, ten to
# the pound, while every merchant, cart and porter in the fiction talks in
# POUNDS. The SD barrel is 460 lb and 4,600 gp weight, and the mule-capacity
# ruling in rules/equipment.md turns on not confusing them. A bare number in
# one column would be a unit kept in somebody's head, which is the shape of
# every error this project is about. Blank is honest -- a guessed weight
